summary: Anantasharma B. G. is an Indology and philosophy scholar who earned a PhD at Central Sanskrit University (2014–2021). He was Head at Veda Vijnana Shodha Samsthana (2019–2023), Chairperson at Amrita Vishwa Vidyapeetham (2023–2025), and Assistant Professor at Chanakya University (2025).

Ananya Vajpeyi specializes in Indology, philosophy, and history/archaeology. She studied at Delhi, JNU, Oxford, Exeter College, and earned her PhD from Chicago (1996–2004). She has held posts at Columbia University and the Centre for the Study of Developing Societies (2011).

Anastasiya Lozhkina works in Indology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy. She studied at Saint Petersburg State University (2007–2009) and Moscow State University (2009–2018), and became a Junior Research Fellow at the Russian Academy of Sciences in 2018.

Anatol Waag studied linguistics and Iranian/Central Asian studies under Johannes Hertel at the University of Leipzig, completing his PhD around 1931. He was an assistant at Leipzig (1932–1939) and worked at the University of Zagreb and Institut für Deutsche Volkskunde.
Anatoli Guenko studied under Jan Niecisław Baudouin de Courtenay and Boris Turayev around 1914–1918.
Anders Hilding Andersson was an Indologist who earned his M.A. (~1871–1875) and Ph.D. (~1875–1878) at Lund University, where he was appointed Docent of Greek Literature in 1879.

Andrea Acri, a scholar of Indology and religious studies, studied under Raffaele Torella, Willem van der Molen, and Arlo Griffiths, completing his PhD at Leiden University (~2006–2011). He held positions at EPHE (2016) and EFEO (2021–2024).

Andrea R. Jain is a scholar of religious studies and Indology who earned her PhD from Rice University in 2010. She has held faculty positions at IUPUI (~2016–2021) and Indiana University Bloomington, where she became a full professor in 2021.

Andrea Schlosser is a scholar of Indology and Buddhist studies who earned her PhD from Free University of Berlin in 2014, studying under Richard G. Salomon and Ingo Strauch. She held researcher positions at the University of Munich and Göttingen Academy of Sciences.
Andreas Bock-Raming, a scholar of Indology and Buddhist studies, studied under Paul Hacker and is attested as a researcher at the Göttingen Academy of Sciences and Humanities in 2026.

Andreas Doctor is a Buddhist studies and Tibetology scholar who completed his PhD at the University of Calgary under Leslie S. Kawamura, alongside traditional teachers including Chökyi Nyima Rinpoche. He held a post at the Rangjung Yeshe Institute.

Andreas Gottlieb Hoffmann was a religious studies and linguistics scholar. He earned his Ph.D. under Wilhelm Gesenius at Halle (~1814–1820), where he became PD in 1822, before serving as Professor of Theology at the University of Jena from 1826.
Andreas N. Kephallenos was an Indology and linguistics scholar who studied at the University of Florence and earned a Ph.D. from the University of Munich.
Andreas Spengel was a scholar in linguistics who studied at the University of Munich (~1856–1859) and Frederick William University Berlin (~1859–1861).
Andree Dominique Messent studied Buddhist studies at the University of Bristol, earning a PhD under the supervision of Paul Williams and studying under Rupert Gethin and Ulrich Pagel.

Andrei Vostrikov was a Tibetology, Indology, and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Saint Petersburg State University under Fyodor Shcherbatskoy and Boris Vladimirtsov. He worked at the Asiatic Museum, Institute of Buddhist Culture, and Leningrad Institute of Living Oriental Languages.

Andrej Evgen’evič Snesarev was a scholar in Iranian/Central Asian studies, history/archaeology, and Indology. Trained at Moscow State University and the General Staff Academy, he served as Head of the General Staff Academy (1919) and Rector of Moscow Institute of Oriental Studies (1922–1924).
Andrew B. Irvine earned a PhD from Boston University in philosophy and religious studies and served as Assistant Professor of Philosophy at Maryville College (attested 2009).
Andrew Garrett is a linguistics and Indology scholar who earned his PhD from Harvard University in 1990. He was appointed Professor at the University of California, Berkeley in 1995.
Andrew Glass is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and linguistics. He studied at Bukkyo University and the University of Washington, completing his PhD in 2006 under Richard G. Salomon.
